cards.text: Israel has just been carried off into Assyria (2 Kings 17:23). Now the king of Assyria brings people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim and settles them in the towns of Samaria. Five different hometowns, all moving onto one street.

cards.question: True or false: The king of Assyria settles these new people in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites.

cards.text: They take over Samaria and move right into its towns. But when they first live there, they don't worship the LORD.

cards.question: The new settlers in Samaria don't worship the LORD, so He sends ___ among them, and some of them are killed.

cards.text: LIONS, friend! I'd have crawled back into my old junk drawer and pulled it shut behind me, but the settlers send word to the king of Assyria instead.

cards.question: The settlers tell the king of Assyria why the lions are killing them. What do they say?

answers.text: We don't know what the God of the land requires
Our towns don't have walls to keep them out
The land sat empty and wild for far too long

cards.text: The king of Assyria has a plan. Somebody has to go live there and teach these people the requirements of the God of the land.

cards.question: The king of Assyria wants someone to go live in Samaria and teach the settlers the requirements of the God of the land. Who does he command them to send?

answers.text: One of the priests carried off from Samaria
One of the prophets living in Judah
One of his own officials from Assyria

cards.question: The priest comes back and lives in Bethel. True or false: He begins teaching the settlers how they should worship the LORD.

cards.text: Problem solved, right? Then the story hits us with the word every storyteller hates to read out loud: nevertheless.

cards.question: The priest is teaching the settlers how to worship the LORD. Nevertheless, the people of each nation keep making their own ___.
The people of each nation in Samaria are making their own gods. Where do they set them up?

answers.text: In the old shrines on the high places
In the priest's house at Bethel
In a new temple from Assyria

cards.text: Each group makes its own: Babylon makes Succoth-benoth, Cuth makes Nergal, Hamath makes Ashima, and the Avvites make Nibhaz and Tartak. And the Sepharvites burn their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
Here's the twist: the new residents do worship the LORD. But that's not the whole picture.

cards.question: The new residents of Samaria worship the LORD. Who do they also appoint to serve in the shrines on the high places?
The new residents worship the LORD, but they also serve their own ___, following the customs of the nations they came from.

cards.text: The LORD AND all their old gods? That's telling your barber he's the only one while you've got four other barbers booked that same week.

cards.question: The settlers worship the LORD and serve their own gods too. True or false: The writer says that counts as worshiping the LORD.
None of the settlers keep the laws the LORD gave the descendants of the man He named Israel. Who is that man?

cards.text: Then the writer looks back at the covenant the LORD made with the Israelites, and what He commanded them.

cards.question: In His covenant with the Israelites, what does the LORD command them first?

answers.text: Do not ever leave the land
Do not trade with the nations

cards.question: Instead, the Israelites are to worship the LORD, who brought them out of ___ with great power and an outstretched arm.

cards.text: He tells them to always keep His laws and never forget the covenant, and then He says it again, and AGAIN: “Do not worship other gods.” Friend, when I set three timers for one batch, that batch is IMPORTANT.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Israelites to worship the LORD their God. What does He promise if they do?

answers.text: He will deliver them from all their enemies
He will give them a king who rules forever
He will send them rain in every season

cards.text: But they would not listen. They kept right on with their former customs.

cards.question: These nations in Samaria worship the LORD but also serve their idols. True or false: Their children and grandchildren finally break the habit.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answer "In a new temple from Assyria" is made up. No temple from Assyria appears anywhere in the Bible. It also sounds less like the Bible than the right answer, "In the old shrines on the high places," so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: Verses 30-31 are a name list, so they count as a long stretch. The summary card still goes through it item by item: every nation paired with every god (Succoth-benoth, Nergal, Ashima, Nibhaz, Tartak, Adrammelech, Anammelech). It should say in a few words what the stretch covers. The child sacrifice to the gods of Sepharvaim could be the one standout detail.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The question asks who the residents appoint to serve in the shrines. "No priests at all" is not the same kind of answer as the other two. It doesn't name anyone, and it doesn't fit the question's wording. It is also shorter and flatter than the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card cites 2 Kings 17:33, which card 3 already asked about and answered. It adds nothing new from the passage. It only repeats what was said, plus a joke, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The barber joke depends on telling the barber "he's the only one." That adds a false promise of loyalty that the text never says the settlers made. The action in the text is serving the LORD and other gods side by side. The comparison is about lying about loyalty, so it doesn't have the same action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The statement "The writer says that counts as worshiping the LORD" is marked false, citing 17:34 ("None of them worship the LORD"). But the writer says plainly in 17:32, 17:33 and 17:41 that they "worshiped the LORD." A baker could argue that "True" is right, so the wrong answer is not false everywhere in the passage. The words "counts as" also add a judgment the text leaves unexplained.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
